Start by maintaining good posture while sitting, standing, or using digital devices. Keep your screen at eye level and avoid looking down at your phone for long periods. Taking short movement breaks every 30–45 minutes helps prevent stiffness and reduces strain on the neck muscles.

Gentle stretching and strengthening exercises for the neck and upper back can improve flexibility and support the cervical spine. Sleeping with a supportive pillow, staying physically active, managing stress, and staying hydrated may also contribute to healthier muscles and joints.

While these measures help many people, persistent neck pain, pain spreading to the shoulder or arm, numbness, tingling, or weakness should be assessed to identify the underlying cause. Recurring neck pain is a common concern among many people in Thane.

Neck pain that keeps returning is often a sign that the underlying cause needs attention. Many people experience temporary relief with rest or medication, but the discomfort may come back if factors affecting the neck are not addressed.

Common reasons for recurring neck pain include poor posture, prolonged screen time, muscle weakness, stress-related tension, previous neck injuries, cervical disc problems, or age-related changes in the spine. Spending long hours looking down at mobile devices or working without proper ergonomic support can place continuous strain on the neck muscles and joints.

Some people may notice stiffness, restricted neck movement, shoulder pain, headaches, or pain spreading toward the arms. In certain cases, symptoms like tingling, numbness, or weakness may indicate nerve irritation and require proper evaluation.

Managing recurring neck pain involves more than temporary pain relief. Improving posture, strengthening neck and upper back muscles, maintaining healthy movement habits, and following appropriate exercises can support long-term spine health.

Patients in Thane often explore whether Pott’s spine can impact leg strength and movement.

Pott’s spine is a type of spinal infection that can affect the bones, discs, and surrounding tissues of the spine. Many patients are concerned whether this condition can cause leg weakness or numbness, especially when symptoms progress over time.

In the early stages, Pott’s spine may cause persistent back pain, stiffness, fatigue, or discomfort. However, if the infection leads to swelling, bone damage, or pressure on the spinal cord or nerves, it can result in nerve-related symptoms such as tingling, numbness, leg weakness, difficulty walking, or changes in balance.

The severity of nerve symptoms depends on the location of infection, the amount of spinal cord or nerve compression, and how early treatment is started. Not every patient with Pott’s spine develops weakness or numbness, but these symptoms should not be ignored.

Diagnosis usually involves a detailed clinical assessment, blood tests, and imaging such as MRI to understand the extent of infection and nerve involvement. Early treatment with appropriate medical care helps control infection, protect nerve function, and reduce the risk of long-term complications.

Timely spine evaluation is important for patients experiencing persistent back pain with neurological symptoms. The goal is to preserve mobility, improve recovery, and support long-term spine health.

Proper diagnosis in Thane helps support safe and timely spine care.

Many patients in Thane explore treatment options for ongoing SI joint-related pain.

The sacroiliac (SI) joint connects the spine to the pelvis and plays an important role in transferring weight and movement between the upper and lower body. When this joint becomes unstable, inflamed, or severely degenerated, it can cause persistent lower back pain, buttock pain, hip discomfort, or pain that worsens while standing, walking, or changing positions.

Most SI joint problems improve with non-surgical treatment such as physiotherapy, activity modification, medications, targeted injections, and strengthening exercises. However, surgery may be considered when symptoms continue for several months despite appropriate conservative care and significantly affect daily activities.

SI joint fusion surgery aims to stabilize the affected joint and reduce abnormal movement that may be contributing to pain. Not every patient with lower back pain requires SI joint fusion. The decision depends on symptom severity, response to previous treatments, overall health, and the impact on quality of life. Accurate diagnosis is essential, as SI joint pain can sometimes mimic other spine or hip conditions. Early assessment helps guide the most appropriate treatment plan and supports long-term mobility and function.

Early evaluation in Thane supports safe and effective long-term care.

Many patients in Thane are concerned about the long-term impact of lumbar canal stenosis on daily life.

Lumbar canal stenosis occurs when the spinal canal in the lower back becomes narrowed, placing pressure on the nerves that travel to the legs. Many patients worry that this condition may eventually lead to paralysis. In most cases, lumbar canal stenosis develops gradually and causes symptoms such as lower back pain, leg pain, numbness, tingling, heaviness in the legs, or difficulty walking long distances.

Complete paralysis from lumbar canal stenosis is uncommon. However, severe and untreated nerve compression can sometimes lead to significant weakness, loss of balance, reduced walking ability, or worsening nerve function. Certain warning signs require prompt medical attention, including progressive leg weakness, loss of bladder or bowel control, or numbness around the groin area.

The severity of symptoms does not always match the degree of narrowing seen on scans, which is why a detailed clinical assessment is important. Treatment may include activity modification, physiotherapy, posture correction, medication, or surgery in selected cases.

Early evaluation helps identify the extent of nerve compression and supports timely treatment decisions. The goal is to preserve mobility, protect nerve function, reduce symptoms, and maintain independence in daily life.

Recurring lower back pain is a common concern among many patients in Thane.

A slip disc can improve with proper treatment, but in some cases, symptoms may return if the spine continues to experience excessive strain. The spine is constantly exposed to daily stress from sitting, lifting, bending, poor posture, obesity, weak core muscles, or physically demanding activities.

Many patients recover well with physiotherapy, medication, posture correction, and lifestyle changes. Recurring symptoms may include lower back pain, leg pain, numbness, tingling, or stiffness similar to earlier episodes. In some cases, the symptoms are mild and temporary, while others may require further medical evaluation.

The focus after slip disc treatment is not only pain relief, but also preventing recurrence through spinal strengthening, posture awareness, ergonomic habits, and guided rehabilitation. Spine reconstruction surgery is carefully planned based on the patient’s spinal condition, symptoms, posture balance, nerve pressure, and overall health. Spine surgeons do not follow a single approach for every patient. Instead, they study imaging scans, spinal alignment, movement patterns, bone quality, and the severity of deformity or instability before deciding the reconstruction strategy.

Conditions such as scoliosis, kyphosis, spinal instability, fractures, infection, or severe disc degeneration may require different surgical planning. The main goal is to restore spinal stability, protect nerves, improve alignment, and reduce pain while helping the patient maintain safe movement and daily function.

Surgeons also consider age, activity level, medical history, muscle strength, and recovery expectations before choosing the most suitable procedure. In some cases, minimally invasive techniques may be possible, while complex deformities may require staged reconstruction surgery.

Every spine behaves differently, which is why individualized planning is important. Careful preoperative evaluation helps reduce surgical risk and improves long-term outcomes. Poor posture linked to prolonged sitting is increasingly common in Thane.

Poor posture may seem harmless at first, but over time it can place continuous stress on the spine, muscles, and joints. Sitting for long hours with rounded shoulders, looking down at mobile phones, or standing unevenly can gradually affect spinal alignment and movement patterns.

In the early stages, posture-related changes are usually flexible and improve with exercise, stretching, and posture correction. However, when poor posture continues for years, the spine and surrounding soft tissues may adapt to that position. This can contribute to exaggerated spinal curves such as kyphosis or lordosis, muscle imbalance, stiffness, and ongoing neck or back pain.

People often notice symptoms like shoulder tightness, forward head posture, fatigue while sitting, or discomfort after long working hours. In some cases, poor posture may also increase pressure on spinal discs and joints, especially when combined with weak core muscles or a sedentary lifestyle.

The good news is that early attention can make a significant difference. Ergonomic adjustments, regular movement, posture training, strengthening exercises, and guided physiotherapy can help improve spinal balance and reduce strain. Intro: Recovery after spine surgery is a common concern among patients in Thane.

After spine surgery, many patients expect nerve pain, numbness, or weakness to disappear immediately. However, nerves usually heal gradually over time. When a nerve has been compressed by a slipped disc, spinal stenosis, or long-standing pressure, it often needs time to recover even after the pressure is removed.

During the healing process, some patients may continue to feel tingling, burning sensations, mild numbness, or intermittent leg or arm pain. This does not always mean the surgery has failed. In many cases, it reflects the natural recovery process of irritated nerves. The speed of healing depends on factors such as the duration of nerve compression, overall health, diabetes, smoking, and the severity of the original condition.

Gentle movement, guided physiotherapy, proper posture, hydration, and adequate sleep all support nerve recovery after spine surgery. Avoiding heavy lifting and following rehabilitation advice are equally important for long-term healing.

Regular follow-up helps monitor recovery and identify whether symptoms are improving as expected. Patience is important, as nerves often heal more slowly than muscles or bones. The focus after surgery is not only pain relief, but also restoring safe movement, stability, and daily function.

Early postoperative care in Thane supports balanced and steady nerve healing.

Many Thane residents experience discomfort during long commutes.

Traveling with sciatica can be uncomfortable, but the right precautions can help you stay mobile and reduce nerve irritation. Sciatica pain usually travels from the lower back to the leg, and long periods of sitting during travel can increase pressure on the spine.

One of the most important tips is to avoid sitting for too long. During long journeys, try to stand, stretch, or walk every 30–45 minutes whenever possible. Using a small lumbar support or rolled towel behind the lower back helps maintain the natural spinal curve and reduces strain.

Choose a comfortable seat with proper back support, and keep your hips and knees at a relaxed angle. Avoid keeping your wallet or bulky items in your back pocket, as this can increase nerve pressure. Staying hydrated and doing gentle ankle and leg movements can also improve circulation.

If pain is active, avoid lifting heavy luggage or sudden twisting movements. A pre-travel spine check with a specialist can help ensure your condition is stable. With simple planning, most people with sciatica can travel safely and comfortably.

🦴 Subtrochanteric Femur Fracture - A True Test of Fracture Fixation

A subtrochanteric femur fracture is a break in the upper part of the femur (thigh) bone, just below the hip joint. These fractures usually occur due to high-energy trauma, most commonly road traffic accidents or major falls 🚗💥

Because of the strong muscle attachments around the hip and thigh, the broken bone fragments are often pulled in different directions by powerful deforming forces, making these fractures difficult to align and stabilize.

🚑 In the emergency setting, the limb is often temporarily stabilized using a Thomas traction splint to reduce pain, bleeding, and further displacement.

🔧 Definitive treatment is usually done with a Long Proximal Femoral Nail (PFN), which is inserted inside the bone to provide strong internal support and maintain proper alignment during healing.

🎯 Goals of treatment:
✅ Restore alignment and stability
✅ Allow early mobilization
✅ Promote proper fracture healing

Early stabilization and surgery are important for better recovery and return to daily activities 💪🦴

🦿 Complex Joint Replacement Surgeries – Restoring Function in Challenging Cases

Not all joint replacements are routine. Some cases require advanced planning, specialized implants, and precise surgical execution to restore mobility and quality of life.

🔹 Case 1 – Revision Total Hip Replacement

A previously well-done cemented hip replacement lasted 35 years 👏
The patient presented with implant loosening and bone loss (lysis).

🔧 Re-do surgery performed with: 
• Extended Trochanteric Osteotomy (ETO)
• Long uncemented stem
• Acetabular augments
• Multi-hole cup

🎯 Aim: Restore stability and address bone loss for long-term function


🔹 Case 2 – Complex Knee Replacement with Instability

• Careful soft tissue balancing
• Knee replacement using primary implants with tibial stem extender

🎯 Aim: Achieve stability, alignment, and balanced knee function


🔹 Case 3 – Knee Replacement with Bone Loss

Severe deformity of the knees with tibial bone loss.

🔧 Reconstruction included:

Complex joint problems need individualized solutions, advanced implants, and surgical precision to achieve the best outcomes.

💪 Restoring mobility. Rebuilding lives.

🦴 Cauda Equina Syndrome – A Spine Emergency

Cauda Equina Syndrome is a serious neurological condition caused by severe compression of the nerves at the lower end of the spinal cord. It requires urgent diagnosis and immediate treatment.

⚠️ Common symptoms may include:
• Weakness or complete paralysis of the ankle and toes 🦶
• Difficulty walking
• Loss of bladder or bowel control 🚨
• Numbness in the lower limbs
• Reduced or absent reflexes

🩺 Diagnosis is made primarily through clinical examination, while MRI is the gold standard investigation to identify the nerve compression.

⏳ This condition is a true surgical emergency.
Urgent spinal decompression surgery is often required to prevent permanent nerve damage and improve chances of recovery.

In this case, the patient was operated at 3 AM within 3 hours of presenting to us, highlighting the importance of timely intervention and coordinated emergency care.

🤝 Team work makes dream work — rapid diagnosis, anesthesia, OT staff, nursing care, and surgical teamwork all play a vital role in managing such emergencies. 💪🩺

🦵 Anterior Cruciate Ligament Tear

The Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) is one of the main stabilizing ligaments inside the knee joint. It connects the femur (thigh bone) to the tibia (shin bone) and helps control knee stability during walking, running, pivoting, and sports activities.

⚠️ ACL tears commonly occur due to:
• Sports injuries 🏃‍♂️
• Sudden twisting movements
• Pivoting or awkward landing after a jump
• Road traffic accidents 🚗💥

Patients may experience pain, swelling, instability, or a “giving way” sensation in the knee.

🔧 Treatment – ACL Reconstruction
ACL reconstruction is performed using a tendon graft. Common graft options include:
• Hamstring tendon
• Patellar tendon
• Peroneus Longus tendon

In this case, a Peroneus Longus graft was harvested and prepared for reconstruction.

🩻 The surgery was performed arthroscopically (keyhole surgery):
✅ Tibial and femoral tunnels were created
✅ The graft was passed and fixed securely
✅ Knee stability was restored

🎯 An equally important part of treatment is rehabilitation.
Proper physiotherapy and guided rehab are essential for:
✅ Regaining movement
✅ Restoring muscle strength
✅ Returning safely to sports and daily activities 💪🦵

🦴 Monteggia Variant Fracture 

A Monteggia fracture variant is a complex elbow injury involving a fracture of the proximal ulna (forearm bone near the elbow) along with a radial head fracture.

These injuries usually occur after a fall on an outstretched hand, road traffic accident, or other high-impact trauma 🚗💥

Patients commonly present with:
⚠️ Pain and swelling around the elbow
⚠️ Difficulty moving the elbow and forearm
⚠️ Reduced ability to lift or rotate the arm

🔧 Treatment:
• The ulna fracture was stabilized using an olecranon plate
• The radial head fracture was fixed with specialized headless screws to preserve the joint surface and movement

🎯 Goal of surgery:
✅ Restore normal elbow anatomy
✅ Achieve stable fixation
✅ Allow early guided rehabilitation

With anatomical reduction and proper rehabilitation, patients can regain good elbow movement and function 💪🦴

🦵 Tibial Plateau Fractures

A tibia plateau / condyle fracture involves the upper part of the tibia bone (shin bone) that forms the knee joint. These injuries affect the joint surface and need careful treatment to restore knee function.

📊 Classification (Schatzker): This case is a Type II (split-depressed) fracture, where the bone is both split and pushed down, affecting the smooth joint surface.

⚠️ How does it occur?
• Road traffic accidents 🚗💥  
• Sports injuries 🏃‍♂️
• Fall from height

🤕 Symptoms
• Pain and swelling around the knee  
• Difficulty or inability to bear weight  
• Reduced knee movement

Due to significant swelling, surgery is sometimes delayed for a few days to allow soft tissues to settle, ensuring safer outcomes and lesser wound complications 

🔧 Treatment: The fracture was fixed using an anterolateral raft plate, which helps support the joint surface, restore alignment, and provide stable fixation.

🎯 Goal: To achieve anatomical joint surface restoration and allow early, guided knee movement for better recovery 💪🦵

🦿 Complex Primary Total Knee Replacement - From Bed-Bound to Standing Again

Advanced Osteoarthritis of the knees can sometimes go beyond pain — causing severe deformity, bone loss, and complete loss of mobility for the patient.

Such cases require a complex surgical procedures using advanced implants with long stems, metal augments for bone loss, and meticulous soft-tissue balancing to restore alignment and function.

This patient had gross deformity of both legs and was barely able to stand or walk for past several months.

A Complex Primary Total Knee Replacement was performed using imported implants to restore alignment, balance, and stability.

✨ Most importantly:

The operated leg was realigned to a near-normal position, and the patient was able to stand again after 6 months 🙏🦿

The second knee is to be operated subsequently, and with proper rehabilitation, the patient is expected to walk with a near-normal gait.

Sometimes, timely surgery doesn’t just relieve pain — it restores dignity, independence, and hope 💙

⚠️ A gentle reminder: Don’t wait until arthritis becomes this severe. Early consultation and timely treatment can help avoid deformity and prolonged immobility.

🦴 Femur Shaft Fracture

A fracture of the shaft of the femur (thigh bone) is a serious injury, most commonly caused by high-energy trauma such as road traffic accidents 🚗💥.

At the scene or in the emergency setting, the limb is often stabilized using a Thomas traction splint to reduce pain and prevent further damage.

⚠️ These fractures can be associated with significant internal bleeding (up to 1–1.5 liters), so patients require urgent stabilization in the emergency room.

🔧 Definitive Treatment
Once the patient is stable, the fracture is treated with Closed Reduction and Internal Fixation using an Interlocking Femur Nail, which provides strong internal support and allows proper healing.

🎯 Goals of treatment:
✅ Stabilize the fracture
✅ Control pain and bleeding
✅ Allow early mobilization and recovery
Prompt and appropriate care is essential for a safe recovery and return to normal activity 💪🦴

🦴 Osteoporosis
Osteoporosis is a condition where bones become weak and brittle, increasing the risk of fractures even after minor falls or injuries.

❓ What causes it?
• Aging 👵👴
• Hormonal changes (especially after menopause)
• Low calcium and vitamin D intake 🥛☀️
• Lack of physical activity
• Certain medications like long term steroids

⚠️ What can happen?
Weak bones can lead to fragility fractures, commonly affecting:
• Hip 🦵
• Wrist ✋
• Spine (leading to back pain or height loss)

🩻 How is it diagnosed?
• Bone density scan (DEXA scan)
• X-rays (if fracture is suspected)

💊 Treatment:
• Calcium and Vitamin D supplements
• Special medications to strengthen bones
• Weight-bearing exercises
• Lifestyle changes (diet, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol)

🚶‍♂️ Fall Prevention Tips:
✔️ Keep floors dry and clutter-free
✔️ Use good lighting, especially at night 🌙
✔️ Wear non-slip footwear
✔️ Install grab bars/handrails
✔️ Regular check-ups for balance and bone health

Early diagnosis and treatment can help prevent fractures and maintain an active, independent life 💪🦴

🦴 Paediatric Both Bone Forearm Fracture

Fractures of both forearm bones (radius and ulna) are among the most common fractures in children, accounting for nearly 40% of all pediatric fractures.

They most often occur after a fall on an outstretched hand while playing. Children usually present with pain, swelling, and visible deformity of the forearm.🤸‍♂️

Diagnosis is confirmed with simple X-rays of the forearm.🩻

Most pediatric forearm fractures can be treated without surgery if the bones can be properly aligned and maintained with closed reduction and plaster casting.

However, surgery may be required if the fracture is significantly displaced or if the alignment cannot be maintained in the cast, especially in children nearing skeletal maturity.

In this case, closed reduction and casting could not maintain proper bone alignment, so the fracture was treated surgically using TENS (Titanium Elastic Nailing System) to stabilize the bones and allow proper healing.🔧

With appropriate treatment and rehabilitation, children usually recover excellent function and return to their normal activities 💪🦴

❓ Patient FAQ Thursday

**My MRI Shows a Disc Bulge. Should I Be Worried?**

One of the most common concerns patients have after an MRI is seeing the words **"disc bulge"** in the report. Fortunately, a disc bulge does **not** automatically mean you have a serious spinal problem or that you need surgery.

A disc bulge is a common MRI finding and is often seen even in people who have no back pain or leg pain. This is why MRI findings should always be interpreted alongside your symptoms and a thorough clinical examination.

Key Things to Know:

✔ A disc bulge is common and may be a part of normal age-related changes.
✔ Many people with disc bulges have no symptoms.
✔ Most patients improve with medications, physiotherapy, activity modification, and guided rehabilitation.
✔ Surgery is required only in selected cases, such as progressive neurological weakness, loss of bladder or bowel control, or persistent disabling pain despite appropriate conservative treatment.

Remember:

**Treat the patient, not just the MRI.**

Your symptoms, physical examination, lifestyle, and functional limitations are far more important than the MRI report alone in deciding the right treatment.

If you've been diagnosed with a disc bulge or slipped disc and are unsure what it means, consult a spine specialist for a comprehensive evaluation and personalized treatment plan.

🩺 **Dr. Siddharth Katkade**
Consultant Spine Surgeon
Bombay Spine Clinic™

⚖️ MYTH vs FACT

❌ Myth: Every Slip Disc Requires Surgery

✅ Fact: Most patients improve without surgery.

A slip disc diagnosis can be worrying, but surgery is not the answer for everyone. In fact, most patients recover successfully with medications, physiotherapy, lifestyle modifications, and guided rehabilitation.

Surgery is generally reserved for selected situations such as persistent severe pain, progressive neurological weakness, or loss of bladder and bowel control.

The most important principle in spine care is to treat the patient's symptoms and clinical condition—not just the MRI report.

If you are experiencing back pain, leg pain, or have concerns about your MRI findings, a proper clinical evaluation can help determine the best treatment approach.

🦴 *SPINE TIP OF THE WEEK*

*THE 10-SECOND SCOLIOSIS CHECK*
*Could Your Child Have a Curved Spine?*

Many children with scoliosis have *no pain at all*, which is why it often goes unnoticed until the curve becomes more obvious.

The good news? A simple 10-second check at home can help identify early warning signs.

👀 *What to look for:*
✅ One shoulder higher than the other
✅ Uneven waistline
✅ One side of the rib cage appearing more prominent
✅ Leaning to one side while standing
✅ Uneven posture in photographs

💡 *Try this simple test:*
Ask your child to stand with feet together, bend forward, and touch their toes while you observe from behind.

Early detection can make a significant difference, especially during growth spurts between *10–16 years of age*.

Remember:
👉 Not every uneven shoulder means scoliosis.
👉 But if you notice any of these signs, it's worth getting the spine evaluated.

A quick 10-second check today could make a lifelong difference tomorrow.

📤 Please share this with parents, teachers, coaches, school groups, and anyone involved in children's health and development. Early awareness matters. 😊

🏃‍♂️ Spine Tip of the Week | The Runner's Paradox

Many runners have excellent cardiovascular fitness and endurance, but running alone may not fully protect against age-related muscle loss (sarcopenia), reduced strength, or declining bone health.

While running trains your heart, strength training helps protect your muscles, bones, joints, and spine.

Benefits of regular strength training for runners:
✅ Improved running efficiency
✅ Better spine support
✅ Reduced injury risk
✅ Stronger muscles and bones
✅ Prevention of age-related muscle loss

A simple goal: For every 3–4 running sessions per week, include at least 2 strength-training sessions. Even 20 minutes twice weekly can make a meaningful difference.

At Bombay Spine Clinic, we encourage runners and active individuals to focus on both endurance and strength for long-term spine health and injury prevention.
